knowledge: Declaration order and first use decide agbcc register allocation; reorder declarations to steer registers.
old_agbcc and agbcc schedule differently; 696 of the 1293 matched functions were built with old_agbcc and may not re-judge under the app's plain agbcc.
register pins (register u32 x asm("r4")) are pret-style and allowed sparingly; they steer allocation without inventing logic.
A .set alias symbol defeats cross-jumping between twin functions (sanctioned for 0x08012B80); the alias lives in the manifest symbols, not in the C.
ldrsb (inline asm) loads a signed byte where the compiler would emit ldrb; used where the ROM proves a signed load.
A byte-match does not guarantee semantic correctness: re-read the disassembly even after a match.
Function extent is the neighbor address (next function start minus this start); never a self-measured window.
The .set alias block must follow the code in a GAS 2.42 file, or the assembler folds the alias into a pool word.
Sub_0803FD68 is called exactly 11 times from 0x0802DB84; a 12th grep hit is a .set stub, not a call.
agbcc compiles Thumb with -mthumb-interwork -O2; the one ARM-mode matched function needs agbcc_arm.

Matched code references the IWRAM base D_02007090 as `extern u8 gUnknown_02007090[];` and derives addresses through a local: `u8 *base = gUnknown_02007090; ... base + 0x18` yields `ldr r0,=0x02007090; adds r0,#0x18`. Writing `gUnknown_02007090 + 0x18` inline instead folds the addend into the literal pool (`ldr r0,=0x020070A8`), drops the adds, and the judge reports "a pointer to gUnknown+0x18 where the original has 0x02007090". Same for D_020070A4, whose -0x14 is D_02007090.

OAM sprite state struct at +0x10 has GBA OAM bitfields (y:8, affineMode:2, objMode:2, mosaic:1, bpp:1, shape:2, x:9, matrixNum:5, size:2, tileNum:10, priority:2, paletteNum:4). In old_agbcc functions judged under agbcc (such as sub_08003154..08003298), initial bitfield clears emit the mask load before the ldrb/ldrh; pre-assigning the mask to a short-lived int local (int m = ~0x20; ((u8*)s)[0x11] = m & ((u8*)s)[0x11];) before subsequent bitfield assignments matches old_agbcc's load order and CSE register reuse under plain agbcc.

In agbcc, reusing a temporary from an earlier part of a function can keep a byte index in a separate register from the scaled address. Verified at sub_0800EA4C: using the same u32 temporary for the initial scene base address and later callback index produced the target ldrb r2 and lsls r0,r2,#2. At UpdateSelectionCursor (0x08021ED4), reusing the u8 selection local for the two position indices gave the target ldrb r3 and lsls r0,r3,#2, while keeping the initial int scan value separate preserved the copy before the phase switch.

In agbcc, reusing an address temporary across independent parts of a function can restore the target allocation without register pins. At 0x0802142C, assigning the address of palette[i] to the same u32 temporary used for the ROM offset table moved that table from r1 to r2 and turned a register-only diff into an exact match.

When a ROM graphics/table reference uses a fixed anchor plus an explicit offset, try an extern symbol for the anchor and a local base before changing control flow. At sub_08007798, declaring D_08172074 as extern and adding 4 to a local base preserved ldr =0x08172074; adds #4, whereas the integer-cast base folded to 0x08172078. Symbolic resource bases likewise preserved the explicit ldrh [base,#0x2C] at sub_08020F70.

notes.text: Converted from the pret-style MMBCC decomp (1293/1677 C-matched, 1306 byte-identical). The layout has 1716 entries, not 1677: it must also include 38 matched functions and 1 ASM function the 1677 denominator excludes, or their src/ files fail validation. The app therefore reports 1293/1703 (75.9%), not 77.1%.

Matched functions use their compiled size in the layout, not the neighbor extent: the app's judge requires the candidate length to equal the target length exactly, and neighbor extents include inter-function zero padding the compiler never emits. Unmatched functions keep the neighbor extent.

696 matched functions were built with old_agbcc in the pret project; the app judges with its pinned agbcc only, so some may not re-judge as matches. The pret compiler per function is noted in each src file's header comment.
